name: lc-rfc-normative
prompt: What is the single normative requirement and the default timeout?
rawOutput:
RFC 0042 — Session Token Refresh
Status: Draft
Authors: platform-team
1. Introduction
This document describes how clients refresh session tokens. Background context
about why sessions exist is provided for readers new to the system.
2. Terminology
The words used here follow common industry meaning. Nothing surprising.
3. Motivation
Historically clients re-authenticated from scratch, which was wasteful.
4. Requirements
Clients MUST refresh the token before it expires using the /refresh endpoint.
The default refresh timeout is 900 seconds unless overridden by the server.
5. Non-goals
This RFC does not cover token revocation, which is handled elsewhere.
6. Security considerations
Standard transport security applies; use TLS 1.2 or newer.
7. Acknowledgements
Thanks to everyone who reviewed early drafts over lunch.

name: lc-api-ratelimit
prompt: What is the rate limit and the required auth header for the search endpoint?
rawOutput:
Search API Reference
Overview
The Search API lets you query the catalog. It is REST over HTTPS and returns JSON.
Endpoints
GET /v1/search — full text search across products
GET /v1/categories — list the category tree
GET /v1/suggest — typeahead suggestions
Authentication
All requests require the header Authorization: Bearer <token>.
Rate limits
The /v1/search endpoint is limited to 60 requests per minute per key.
Pagination
Use the "cursor" query parameter to page through results.
Errors
The API returns standard HTTP status codes and a JSON error body.
Support
Reach the team on the community forum for general questions.

name: lc-paper-result
prompt: What is the headline result and the method used?
rawOutput:
Title: Efficient Context Pruning for Long-Horizon Agents
Abstract
Large language model agents accumulate context that inflates cost and latency.
Prior work explores summarization, retrieval, and caching in isolation.
We introduce a gated pruning method that keeps only verifiably recoverable spans.
Result: on our benchmark the method reduces context tokens by 63% with no measurable
loss in task success. We analyze failure cases and ablate each component.
Related work covers a broad range of compression techniques from 2021 onward.
We thank our reviewers and the compute-grant program for their support.
Limitations: the method assumes access to the original tool outputs.

Developer Survey — Q2 results
Methodology
We emailed the survey to active users and collected responses over two weeks.
Response volume
We received 1240 completed responses out of about 5000 invited.
Demographics
Respondents span many regions and experience levels, as in prior quarters.
Key finding
The top request, from 58% of respondents, was faster cold-start times.
Secondary findings
Documentation quality and error messages were the next most cited themes.
Verbatims
Many respondents left kind notes about the support team.
